steps: UI: test wallet m4Ac… (this build's admin) clicked Admin Initialise on /admin/
UI: Admin Deposit 0.1 SOL into the reward vault
UI: main page, 0.05 SOL for 7 days, Stake SOL; the portfolio then showed 0.05 SOL / 7 days
Script: initialize apy_rate 100 (what the admin page sends)
Script: admin deposits 0.2 SOL of rewards
Script: B stakes 0.1 SOL for 20 s
Script: B calls config (no admin check; it creates and sets B's own vault, not the admin's)
Script: admin withdraws the whole vault balance (rent included)
evidence.functional_evidence: stake landed from the app; unstake after the (short) lock landed from the script. The 7-day UI minimum is a limit, not a broken unstake.
evidence.ui_check: Driven in headless Chromium with an injected Wallet Standard test wallet (tests/devnet/wallet_click.py colosseum, log tests/devnet/logs/ui-clicks-2026-11-10.jsonl): initialise, deposit, config, stake and claim went through the app's own buttons, and the early unstake was refused by the program.

limitations: The shortest stake in the app is 7 days, so unstaking after the lock was run from the script (20 s stake). apy_rate is used as a plain multiplier: the admin page's default of 100 pays 100× the stake per year (the script's 0.1 SOL earned 6,024 lamports in about 12 s). Rewards, stakes and the admin's deposit share one vault, and withdraw sends its whole balance, rent included, to the admin, which closes the vault (seen in the script). The APY shown on the main page is a fixed '50%' label. config has no admin check, but it can only touch the caller's own vault.
